page_title: Realtime Django Part 1: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Introduction and Setup)

summary.title: Realtime Django Part 1: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Introduction and Setup)
summary.one_liner: Part 1 of a series introducing the goals, prerequisites and project setup for a real-time Django chat app using WebSockets, RabbitMQ, django-channels and a Vue.js frontend.
keywords: connect vue spa to django backend
takeaways: Understand the goal: using WebSockets to add realtime features to a Django application.
Learn the outline of building a simple 'mini pusher' broadcast system with RabbitMQ.
See that the tutorial covers token-based auth and connecting a Vue.js SPA to a Django REST backend.
Set up a new Django project named chatire with a virtual environment, migrations and the dev server.
Know that django-channels is now the recommended WebSocket approach, replacing the original uWSGI version; part 2 covers auth with djoser.
summary.summary: This is the first part of a multi-part tutorial on building a realtime chat application with Django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js. It lists prerequisites (familiarity with Django, the Getting Started guide and the polling app, and basic JavaScript and Vue.js), and notes that the original uWSGI-based WebSocket layer was extended to use django-channels in March 2021. The page then covers the learning goals and a short installation section: creating a virtual environment, installing Django, starting a project called chatire, running migrations and starting the development server. Code blocks were not captured in the page text, so the exact commands are not included here.
